recall.question: How do shells map to items, and what checks the depth gate?
recall.answer: Shells 0-1 live in items 1-2, shells 2-3 in items 3-6, shell 4 in item 7, shell 5 in item 8, shell 6 in item 9, shell 7 in item 11, shell 8 in item 10, shell 9 in item 12, shell 10 in item 13(c). Item 13 checks the depth gate.

keyTerms.definition: A learned stand-in for the human. It compresses pairwise judgments into one scalar per response.
The leash to the reference policy. Beta sets the leash length: short leash, small changes.
Trimming the update so no single token moves the objective more than (1+eps) times its advantage.
Direct preference optimization. It reparameterizes reward as beta*log(pi/ref) and needs no sampler or value net.
Return minus baseline. Subtracting the baseline keeps the gradient unbiased with lower variance.
Optimizing the proxy instead of the truth. Goodhart's law: the measure becomes the target, then moves.

recall.question: What are DPO's three assumptions?
recall.answer: Bradley-Terry preferences, the optimal policy has the KL-constrained form, and pairs are iid.

recall.question: How does GRPO avoid training a critic?
recall.answer: The group is its own control: better-than-siblings responses are upweighted, worse are downweighted. The baseline only exists when the group varies.

recall.question: Why are verifiable rewards attractive, and what is their catch?
recall.answer: They are programs: unit tests, answer matchers, proof checkers. They never drift or flatter, but they punish formatting deviations as harshly as wrong answers.
